transcript_full_pass: Chicago tried to move the bean seven inches. The bean declined. How many people would it actually take? The real one is structurally supported, so imagine a loose bean. Assume friction resists half its weight, and each person pushes 300 newtons. That's 490,000 newtons, about 1,600 perfectly coordinated people. Perfectly is doing a lot of work. Opposite pushes cancel. Angled ones only partly help. Most people can't reach it. Seven inches is a distance, not the starting force. The real bean needs an anchoring calculation. Chicago brought the squad. The bean brought a foundation. Follow Media Diet for the physics behind the headlines.
